Carlos Bringuier was the Cuban exile leader in New Orleans who clashed with Lee Harvey Oswald in the summer of 1963, in a street argument and then a radio debate. He later set down his anti-Castro case in the book Red Friday, published in Chicago by Charles Hallberg and Company.

This review weighs the book, and the reviewer is unsure what to make of it. He questions whether it has real substance or is the work of 'a nut of the extreme radical right.'
